options.text: It creates a triangle with constrained side lengths.
options.feedback: The diagonal creates a triangle when its lengths and joints hold.

options.text: It makes all connections infinitely strong.
options.feedback: The brace does not make joints infinitely rigid or strong.
A brace carries and constrains forces; it does not eliminate them.

blocks.markdown:
## What to use

A hinged four-sided frame can change angles while keeping side lengths. A diagonal constrains that motion through a triangular geometry. Real performance also depends on connections, member behavior and anchorage; a classroom brace is not a structural design.

blocks.work: Its square diagonal is 5 units. A fixed 5-unit diagonal ties those three lengths together.
blocks.answer: The triangle constrains shape when its members and connections hold their lengths.

options.feedback: One-quarter inch is the fall per foot, not per four-foot run.
Four feet times one-quarter inch per foot gives one inch.
Four is the run in feet; multiply it by the slope.

blocks.markdown:
## What to use

An estimate is useful when followed by a measurement. Keep prediction, measured result and revised explanation as separate records. A slope that looks nearly level can still have a meaningful fall over a long run.

## What to use

blocks.prompt: Follow the quantities and units.

blocks.answer: Required depth 6 5/8 in. Use the different values on Case B for the assessed task.

blocks.markdown:
## Case B - Route the drain through the service zone

This is a dry classroom coordination model, not an installation approval or permission to alter framing. Original horizontal run is 18 ft; available service-zone depth is 8 in. Required slope is at least 1/4 in/ft. Pipe OD is 2 3/8 in. Minimum top and bottom clearances are 3/4 in each. All vertical dimensions use the zone top as datum. Two changes may be proposed for review: shorten the run to 16 ft, or deepen the zone to 8 1/2 in while keeping the 18-ft run. Other fittings, access and connections are not specified.

| Condition | Value |
|---|---|
| Original horizontal run | 18 ft |
| Available zone depth | 8 in |
| Required slope | 1/4 in/ft minimum |
| Pipe outside diameter | 2 3/8 in |
| Top / bottom clearance | 3/4 in each |
| Alternative 1 | 16-ft run; 8-in zone |
| Alternative 2 | 18-ft run; 8 1/2-in zone |

1. List fixed requirements and the two changes available for review.
2. Calculate original fall, required depth and quantified conflict. Reject an unsupported slope reduction.
3. Evaluate both alternatives, including remaining depth margin.
4. Draw a plan and longitudinal section for your proposed route: flow, horizontal run, slope, datum, elevations and outside envelope.
5. Write an RFI explaining what another trade must confirm before the proposal could be used.
